title: Altermagnetic Anomalous Hall Effect and Spin--Edge-Locked Chiral Modes in a Modified Kane--Mele--Hubbard Model
abstract: We establish a correlation-driven route to the altermagnetic anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and its associated \emph{spin--edge-locked} edge states in a modified Kane--Mele--Hubbard model. Using dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), we show that, at half-filling, increasing the Hubbard interaction drives the system from a metallic paramagnetic phase hosting antichiral edge states into an insulating in-plane Néel-type antiferromagnetic phase, in which a residual antiunitary symmetry forbids the AHE. Hole doping induces a spin-flop transition to an out-of-plane Néel-type antiferromagnetic phase, thereby breaking this symmetry and generating a finite anomalous Hall conductivity that persists into the strongly correlated regime. Distinct from a conventional spin-polarized Hall response in ferromagnets, the altermagnetic AHE receives equal and additive contributions from the two symmetry-related spin sectors and is accompanied by spin--edge-locked chiral states. Our results demonstrate that carrier doping and spin-rotationally invariant Hubbard interactions are sufficient to realize the altermagnetic AHE, without invoking an explicitly Ising-like interaction, and provide a realistic microscopic route toward its realization in correlated transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers.
summary: This theoretical study uses DMFT on the Kane-Mele-Hubbard model to predict the altermagnetic Anomalous Hall Effect (AHE) in correlated TMD monolayers. The key finding is that doping drives the system into a specific antiferromagnetic phase that breaks necessary symmetries, thereby generating a measurable AHE. This work provides a realistic, correlation-based mechanism for realizing such topological transport phenomena.
main_problem: The paper establishes a correlation-driven route to the altermagnetic anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and its associated spin--edge-locked edge states.
main_result: Hole doping induces a spin-flop transition to an out-of-plane Néel-type antiferromagnetic phase, which breaks symmetry and generates a finite AHE, distinct from conventional ferromagnetism.
method: The study employs Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) to incorporate dynamical electronic correlations into the analysis of the Kane-Mele-Hubbard model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a modified Kane-Mele-Hubbard (AKMH) model, applied to transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers, incorporating hopping, spin-orbit coupling, and an onsite Hubbard interaction.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity (sigma_xy), magnetic phases (paramagnetic, xy-AF, z-AF), and spin--edge-locked chiral edge states.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction strength (U), electron doping level (n), and spin-orbit coupling (lambda).
main_assumptions: The DMFT approximation is used, which neglects nonlocal quantum fluctuations; the analysis contrasts results derived from spin-rotationally invariant interactions versus Ising-like ones.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the honeycomb structure, the evolution of local magnetization and energy differences across magnetic transitions, and momentum-resolved spectral functions showing edge-localized modes.
paper_structure: The work systematically analyzes the system's behavior by varying the Hubbard interaction (U) and doping level (n). It first establishes the transition from a paramagnetic to an antiferromagnetic phase, then details how doping drives the system into the symmetry-breaking z-AF phase, which is responsible for the measurable AHE.
why_interesting: The focus on correlation-driven topological phenomena (AHE) in strongly correlated materials like TMDs provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding emergent quantum states beyond simple band theory.
